task.goal: Choose one design direction whose architecture makes JevRev's evidence-led routing useful, inspectable, and visually specific.
task.context: The page targets developers using coding agents. It must preserve the frozen copy and behaviors in benchmarks/one-shot-showcase/input.json. The existing hand-drawn skull is a strong anchor. The page is a public landing page, not an application dashboard.

constraints.text: Preserve the frozen copy and add no performance, cost, customer, or production claims
Use local HTML, CSS, JavaScript, system fonts, and the existing banner only
Support keyboard focus, responsive layouts, light and dark modes, and reduced-motion preferences
Every interaction must clarify a real decision or evidence relationship
Fit within a static MVP and remain easy to inspect locally

success.text: A first-time reader can explain Sift, Probe, and Decide from the page
The proposal ranking and evidence reversal are visibly connected
The composition feels native to JevRev and preserves the skull anchor
Text and interaction carry useful information without decorative clutter
Desktop, mobile, keyboard, theme, and reduced-motion states can be checked without external services

candidates.title: Black violet interface grid
candidates.summary: Use heavy sans typography, black-violet gradients, repeated rectangular frames, and a familiar feature grid.
candidates.mechanism: Center the value proposition inside nested sharp frames, repeat equal bordered modules for the workflow and proof, and use a violet gradient for primary actions.
assumptions: Familiar AI tool conventions reduce scanning effort
Repeated frames create enough visual structure without imagery
risks: The page may remain interchangeable with generic generated landing pages
Equal modules can obscure the evidence reversal
validation: Verify anchors, focus, theme, and command copy

candidates.title: Painterly evidence dossier
candidates.summary: Build a literary noir case file where the skull, decision stages, and ranking reversal share one functional visual language.
candidates.mechanism: Use the hand-drawn skull as a cropped hero anchor, a restrained paper and rust palette, serif case headings, sharp dossier borders, a keyboard-accessible Sift-Probe-Decide rail, and a proposal-versus-evidence lens that changes the candidate route in place.
assumptions: The existing illustration can support a painterly case-file language
Developers benefit when interaction exposes the causal transition from proposal to evidence
risks: Expressive material treatment can reduce legibility if contrast or texture is not controlled
High information density must collapse carefully on mobile
validation: Test all decision and evidence states with mouse and keyboard
Inspect hero, workflow, proof, and install hierarchy at 1440px and 390px
Verify theme parity, reduced motion, console, focus, and overflow

candidates.title: Terminal proof stack
candidates.summary: Lead with executable commands and arrange the case as a dense monochrome terminal transcript.
candidates.mechanism: Use a documentation shell, monospace typography, command-first onboarding, collapsible probe logs, and a compact final decision block.
assumptions: Developer audiences will privilege inspectability over brand expression
Command density can make evidence feel concrete
risks: A terminal motif can simulate product output instead of explaining it
The skull and broader brand voice become incidental
validation: Check that every displayed command maps to the committed workflow
Inspect reading order and mobile wrapping
Verify no simulated result is mistaken for live output

candidates.title: Minimal documentation masthead
candidates.summary: Use a quiet documentation layout with the install command first and a compact proof below.
candidates.mechanism: Lead with short technical copy and installation, present workflow as restrained text sections, then place the existing banner beside a concise ranking reversal.
assumptions: Immediate setup is the primary reader need
Minimal styling will keep attention on the product boundary
risks: The decision model can read as undifferentiated documentation
The page may not make the route reversal memorable
